text: You can see Africa from Europe. It's 14 kilometers away.
So why can't you drive there?
That's shorter than Manhattan.
The Channel Tunnel is 50 kilometers.
So 14 should be easy.
Right?
Here's the catch.
The problem isn't the distance.
It's the depth.
Up to 900 meters.
Drop the Burj Khalifa in the middle and it vanishes.
Add racing currents, colliding tectonic plates
and one of the world's busiest shipping lanes. So how do you join two continents?
Rewind to 1928 a German architect Hermann Zurgel had a plan. Damn the
strait and lower the whole Mediterranean by up to 200 meters. New land about the
size of France. Nobody asked the fish. It never happened. So in 1979 Spain and
Morocco agreed to link up. Spain excited, eager.
Let's build it! Morocco, cheerful, keen. Deal. When do we start?
Spain, sheepish, stalling. Right after one more study.
47 years later, one study finally came back different.
It's possible! A rail tunnel diving 475 meters below the sea.
4 times deeper than the channel tunnel. Spain to Morocco in 30 minutes.
Ready by 2035? Maybe 2040? Too late for the 2030 World Cup they're co-hosting.
Or just wait. Africa is creeping toward Europe a few millimeters a year.
Give it millions of years and geologists expect the gap to close.
For free. Until then, don't worry.
